subject: I almost bought the wrong rental
preheader: the deal looked great. the lender disagreed.
headline: A story about ignoring DSCR and almost paying 8% over cap.
body: Back in 2019 I found a duplex in a market I won't name. Brick. Updated. Tenants in place. $1,650 each side, $325k asking. I ran the cap rate in my head — felt like a 7-something — and decided I loved it.
I didn't run DSCR. I figured the lender would tell me if there was a problem. Big mistake. I drove to the property twice. Walked the units. Sent the LOI. Got verbal acceptance. Then went to my bank.

DSCR came back at 1.09. Their floor was 1.25. The loan I'd been modeling in my head (75% LTV, 30-year, 6.5%) didn't exist for this property. The only option was 65% LTV with a rate bump. My cash-on-cash collapsed from a daydream 11% to a real 4.2%.

I walked away. The lesson wasn't 'lenders are picky.' The lesson was that I'd let myself fall in love with a deal before I'd run the numbers a lender would actually use. Eight percent over a defensible cap rate because I felt good walking the units.
Run the numbers first. Walk the property second. TrueCap exists so the version of me from 2019 spends 60 seconds checking before he drives four hours.
